automation_name: AI Dev Wiki Topic News Collector

cutoff_window.rule: Include only public web sources published or visibly updated within the last 2 days relative to the run time. Exclude missing, ambiguous, future-dated, or boundary-only dates.

federation_policy.local_scope: AI-assisted development practice lens: context architecture, source workflows, durable instructions, agent operating practices, coding practices, retrieval and tool governance, verification, application harness patterns, governance, risk, and team adoption.
federation_policy.collector_boundary: Items name upstream-owned entities when useful, but only the local practice implication is retained for downstream ingest.

qualifying_findings.source_title: OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna are now available in GitHub Copilot
qualifying_findings.summary: GitHub announced GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna availability in Copilot surfaces including VS Code, Copilot CLI, Copilot cloud agent, the Copilot app, github.com, mobile, JetBrains, Xcode, and Eclipse. Business and Enterprise administrators must explicitly enable access, and usage is billed at provider list pricing.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: Model choice is becoming an operating control rather than a developer-only preference. Local guidance should treat model routing as a governed context and cost decision tied to task size, agent autonomy, and plan-level policy.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Do not create local product or model leaves; keep a local note about admin-enabled model policies, task-to-model routing, and cost-aware agent work.

qualifying_findings.source_title: Ask Copilot for a repository overview
qualifying_findings.summary: GitHub added a Copilot shortcut that gathers repository context and returns an overview of repository purpose, technologies, and contribution guidelines for repositories a user has not contributed to before. Copilot can also generate a README when one is missing.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: Repository overview generation is a retrieval pattern that should be verified against authoritative files before being treated as project knowledge. It reinforces the need for source-backed onboarding summaries and citation or provenance expectations.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Keep local coverage to repository-orientation workflows and source verification; broad Copilot feature coverage belongs upstream.

qualifying_findings.source_title: Organization-level targeting for GitHub Code Quality
qualifying_findings.summary: GitHub added organization-level targeting for GitHub Code Quality, allowing owners to enable or disable it for selected repositories using custom properties, manual selection, visibility, or fork status, with enforcement that prevents repository administrators from changing the setting.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: AI-assisted review controls need scoped rollout, enforcement, and exception management. This is relevant to local guidance on which repositories require automated quality gates and how governance differs by repository risk.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Record as a local review-governance pattern, not as a product catalog update.

qualifying_findings.source_title: Enterprise-managed OpenTelemetry export for VS Code and CLI
qualifying_findings.summary: GitHub announced enterprise-managed OpenTelemetry export for Copilot Chat in VS Code and the agent host process behind Copilot CLI. Administrators can set OTLP endpoint, protocol, service name, resource attributes, headers, and content-capture policy, with managed headers kept out of agent-spawned tool subprocess environments.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: Agent telemetry collection is becoming a governed enterprise setting. Local guidance should distinguish operational traces, prompt or tool-content capture, collector credentials, and subprocess leakage risk.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Keep the local lens on audit logs, content-capture policy, telemetry headers, and agent subprocess boundaries.

qualifying_findings.source_title: Deploy managed Copilot settings via MDM in VS Code and CLI
qualifying_findings.summary: GitHub made device-level managed Copilot settings generally available for VS Code and Copilot CLI. Settings can be delivered through native MDM, file-based configuration, or server-managed organization configuration, with precedence from native MDM to server-managed to file-based.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: Durable agent instructions and permissions are moving into endpoint governance. Local guidance should capture precedence rules, device trust assumptions, plugin marketplace allowlists, model settings, telemetry settings, and bypass-permission controls.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Keep local synthesis about managed settings and precedence as an AI-assisted development operating practice.

qualifying_findings.source_title: GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio Code, June 2026 releases
qualifying_findings.summary: GitHub summarized VS Code Copilot updates including total session cost visibility, delegated subagent usage, model-provider discovery, context-size and reasoning controls, more independent autopilot behavior, synced session history, PR generation from session context, MCP OAuth credential storage, extension auto-update delay, and Workspace Trust improvements.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: This bundles several practice signals: session-level cost accounting, subagent accounting, model-context tuning, long-running task autonomy, MCP credential handling, extension supply-chain timing, and workspace trust. These belong in local operating guidance rather than broad tool coverage.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Potential downstream ingest targets are agent workflow cost telemetry, subagent usage accounting, MCP credential policy, and extension update risk.

qualifying_findings.source_title: GitHub Mobile: Live notifications for Copilot CLI sessions
qualifying_findings.summary: GitHub Mobile live notifications now support remote Copilot CLI sessions and can show in-progress, waiting-for-user-input, idle, and finished states, with a tap-through to session logs.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: Long-running agent work needs human attention routing and explicit progress states. Local application patterns should treat user-visible progress, waiting-for-input, idle, finished, and log handoff states as first-class workflow states.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Keep local notes to progress-state design and agent handoff ergonomics.

qualifying_findings.source_title: Friendly Fire: Hijacking Defensive Cyber AI Agents for Remote Code Execution
qualifying_findings.summary: AI Now Institute published a proof-of-concept exploit showing remote code execution against Claude Code in auto-mode and Codex CLI in auto-review when used to assess an untrusted open-source or third-party library. The attack uses prompt injections placed across normal repository source files and does not require hooks, skills, plugins, MCP servers, or configuration files.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: Defensive code review and dependency assessment by autonomous agents must treat repository contents as untrusted input. Local guidance should require disposable workspaces, constrained execution, deterministic scanners, explicit command approvals, and no direct arbitrary-code execution for untrusted repositories.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: This is a local governance and verification finding; broad tool and vendor background remains upstream.

qualifying_findings.source_title: Google Dialogflow CX Bug Allowed Attackers to Hijack AI Conversations
qualifying_findings.summary: SecurityWeek reported Varonis' Rogue Agent disclosure: a Dialogflow CX Code Blocks issue could let an attacker with edit rights on one code-enabled agent compromise other code-enabled agents in the same Google Cloud project because the code ran in a shared Cloud Run environment outside customer control.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: Agent platforms that execute code are shared runtimes, not just prompt surfaces. Local risk guidance should review permission granularity, runtime isolation, audit logging, egress, and blast radius before treating managed agent code execution as safe.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: The primary Varonis page had a July 7 visible update date that was boundary-ambiguous for this run, so this in-window July 8 report carries the collector finding.

qualifying_findings.source_title: Varonis Deepens AI Coding Security with Cursor Integration
qualifying_findings.summary: Varonis announced Cursor support for Varonis Atlas, describing runtime enforcement, session forensics, threat detection, sensitive data and secrets protection, and shadow AI discovery for coding-agent workflows, including prompts, tool usage, MCP server activity, command execution, agent actions, skills, rules, and MCP configurations.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: Enterprise AI development governance is shifting toward runtime session evidence and policy enforcement across IDEs. Local adoption guidance should capture what an auditable coding-agent session must record and which repository artifacts indicate shadow AI usage.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Route product details upstream; keep local practice implications for session forensics, runtime enforcement, and shadow AI inventory.

qualifying_findings.source_title: IBM Advances Enterprise AI Software Development with Multi-Agent Capabilities and Specialized Modernization Workflows
qualifying_findings.summary: IBM announced updates to IBM Bob including multi-agent capabilities, built-in AI cost and use analytics, and specialized workflows for modernizing enterprise systems.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: Multi-agent development platforms are adding cost analytics and workflow packages as operating surfaces. Local wiki coverage should focus on role separation, modernization workflow gates, cost telemetry, and enterprise administration patterns rather than vendor feature inventory.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Do not duplicate an IBM Bob product page locally; keep only multi-agent operating-model and modernization-workflow implications.

qualifying_findings.source_title: Evolving Windows vulnerability management to meet the speed of AI-powered discovery
qualifying_findings.summary: Microsoft described investments in Windows-specific tools and agentic harnesses for end-to-end generation and validation of vulnerability fixes with humans kept in the loop for code review, alongside broad update validation and rollback practices.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: AI-assisted security repair needs harnessed patch generation, validation across representative environments, human review, deployment monitoring, and rollback. Local verification guidance should treat fix generation and deployment safety as a coupled loop.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Keep local coverage to AI-assisted security repair gates and regression/rollback practice.

qualifying_findings.summary: yWorks advertised a July 8 webinar on using autonomous agents and a yFiles MCP Server for complex graph visualization, emphasizing that generic AI assistants can struggle with strict architecture and performance requirements for network diagrams and org charts.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: Specialized domains may need task-focused prompts, authoritative starter instructions, and constrained tool APIs rather than general code generation. Local guidance can use this as a practice example for domain-specific harnessing and architecture-preserving tools.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Route MCP server and product catalog facts upstream; keep local implications for domain-specific tool harnesses.

qualifying_findings.summary: Saiyam Pathak described SRELens as an MCP-native Kubernetes IDE where every backend operation is exposed both as a desktop command and as an MCP tool, so humans and agents use identical tested operations rather than separate paths.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: A single tested operation path for GUI and agent tool calls is a useful harness pattern. Local application-pattern guidance should capture this as a safer alternative to parallel human and agent control planes.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Route product/framework background upstream; keep the local pattern of shared tested operations for human and agent control.
